transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-15
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes (recording ends at ~14:48)
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE); Liam Chen (Redwood SE); Priya Nair (Aurora CISO); Tom Alvarez (Aurora Security Eng); Samir Gupta (Aurora Head of Platform)

Summary:
Quick security review focused on encryption at-rest and in-transit, KMS options (hosted KMS vs BYOK vs HSM), key rotation/rotation policies, and audit logging. Customer wants strong BYOK story and clarity on where plaintext ever exists, support for external HSM (PKCS#11), and SOC2/ISO evidence. Next steps: send certs, BYOK guide, schedule HSM deep-dive.

Topics:
- Encryption at rest: disk/file vs envelope encryption
- In transit: TLS, mTLS between components
- KMS: Redwood managed KMS, cloud KMS integrations, BYOK flow
- HSM: on-prem HSM / cloud HSM / PKCS#11 support
- Audit logs, key access, SSO/RBAC implications

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro — I'm Maya, AE on the account. we have Liam from security and infra.
[00:07] Priya: Hi all, I'm Priya. we've got a handful of compliance asks up front — SOC2, ISO, and then more detailed key mgmt questions.
[00:13] Tom: Tom here. biggest thing for us is BYOK + HSM support and ensuring no plaintext leaves our control. also curious about audit trails.
[00:20] Liam: Great, we'll go through high level and then dig in. quick note — I'll mention typical caveats around caching and model artifacts.
[00:27] Samir: timeline — we're aiming to start a pilot in May, full rollout H2. need to validate KMS and deployment model asap.
[00:34] Maya: Ok, first, SOC2/ISO certs — we can send those immediately. for the encryption conversation, Redwood supports in-transit TLS across all services, and we offer both Redwood-managed keys and BYOK where customers bring keys from their cloud KMS or external HSM.
[00:49] Priya: when you say BYOK, do you support keys in AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and also external HSMs? we need attestation for HSM.
[00:56] Liam: Yes, we integrate with AWS KMS and GCP KMS for envelope encryption; we also support BYOK with external HSMs via PKCS#11 for Redwood Private deployments. for hosted customers we typically do cloud-KMS BYOK (you keep the root key), for Private we can plug into your HSM cluster.
[01:12] Tom: Can you walk through the envelope encryption flow? where is the DEK (data encryption key) generated and stored?
[01:19] Liam: Sure — high level: the data encryption key (DEK) is generated in the runtime node, used to encrypt objects (e.g., model cache, persistent storage), then the DEK is encrypted with a KMS-managed key (KEK). the encrypted DEK is stored alongside the data. Redwood does not persist DEKs unencrypted. if BYOK is used the KEK never leaves your KMS/HSM.
[01:40] Priya: so plaintext DEK exists in memory on the node when encrypt/decrypt operations happen, right? any way to avoid that?
[01:47] Liam: yes, DEK exists transiently in node memory during crypto ops. we minimize surface by using ephemeral memory, mlock where available, and immediately zeroing buffers after use. for HSM-backed operations you can perform wrap/unwrap via HSM so KEK material stays in HSM and only wrapped blobs come back.
[02:06] Samir: how does this interact with Redwood caching? we've got concerns about KV cache with long-lived plaintext in memory.
[02:13] Liam: KV cache is in memory for performance. we encrypt persisted cache shards with envelope encryption. in-memory keys are short-lived and rotated; we also have options to reduce in-memory TTL. we'll share cache-specific configs.
[02:26] Tom: For BYOK, do you support key rotation initiated from our KMS? example: we rotate customer root keys every 90 days — how does Redwood handle rewrapping?
[02:35] Liam: We support rewrap workflows. when a KEK rotates, our service will call your KMS/HSM to rewrap DEKs — we can do a bulk rewrap or on-access rewrap. we recommend scheduled bulk rewrap during maintenance windows for predictable performance.
[02:50] Priya: Audit logs: we need proof of who requested unwraps and when, for our auditors. do you provide detailed KMS access logs and per-request metadata?
[02:58] Maya: Yes — for Private deployments we surface detailed audit logs: key unwrap events, actor, timestamp, request origin (IP), and the KMS call ID. for hosted we provide a set of audit exports and you can route logs to your SIEM via syslog/S3.
[03:15] Tom: Are logs tamper-evident or signed?
[03:18] Liam: We support write-once storage for logs in Private; we can also sign logs with a separate key and provide log hashes on request to support tamper evidence.
[03:27] Samir: HSM details — does Redwood support CloudHSM (AWS) or Cloud HSMs from GCP/Azure, and do you support FIPS 140-2/3 certs?
[03:36] Liam: We integrate with AWS CloudHSM and Google Cloud HSM for Private setups; FIPS compliance depends on the HSM offering. Redwood itself does not claim FIPS for customer HSMs — the HSM vendor's cert covers that. for our managed KMS we use FIPS-compliant primitives where available; we can document the exact crypto modules.
[03:56] Priya: For audit, we need key custodians defined and separation of duties. can RBAC map to our SSO (SAML)?
[04:03] Maya: Yes, Redwood supports SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning; RBAC roles can be mapped to SSO groups. for Private we can also integrate with your LDAP/AD.
[04:13] Tom: about encryption in transit — is mutual TLS supported between Redwood components and our private VPC?
[04:19] Liam: yes, mTLS is supported for Private; hosted API uses TLS 1.2/1.3 with cert pinning where needed. for dedicated/private we can mutually authenticate service endpoints.
[04:30] Samir: any additional latency when using HSM for wrap/unwrap? we need numbers to evaluate throughput impact.
[04:36] Liam: good question — there's a small latency hit on wrap/unwrap calls (tens to low hundreds of milliseconds depending on HSM and network). we typically recommend caching wrapped DEKs locally so unwraps are infrequent; we'll include a small benchmark and sample numbers for common HSMs.
[04:53] Priya: what about model artifacts and tokenizer files — do you encrypt those at rest with the same envelope flow?
[04:59] Liam: yes, model artifacts stored on disk are encrypted with DEKs and the DEKs are wrapped with KEKs. for hosted customers we handle artifact storage in encrypted buckets; for Private we can point at customer-managed storage.
[05:10] Maya: quick aside — some of our docs call out "Redwoo Dedicated" in transcripts — ignore that, thats just transcription noise ha.
[05:16] (laughter)
[05:20] Tom: any product limitations we should be aware of? e.g., are there operations that require Redwood to have plaintext access to data keys?
[05:27] Liam: No operation requires us to store plaintext DEKs on disk. runtime nodes will have transient plaintext in memory. one caveat: some analytics/tracing may include metadata; we can redact payloads. if you need zero-plaintext on our side you'd likely need an architecture where crypto operations are entirely on your side and we only receive encrypted blobs — that's doable in Private but limits features like prefix caching.
[05:51] Priya: need clarity on the exact RBAC role that can perform key unwraps — is that an operator role?
[05:57] Liam: yes, unwrap rights are granted to specific service accounts and admin roles. we can provide a mapping of Redwood roles to actions (unwrap, rewrap, rotate, grant).
[06:06] Samir: For regulatory reasons, we need data residency in EU and keys also to remain in EU. is regional KMS allowed?
[06:12] Maya: yes, we can restrict key usage to regional KMS endpoints and ensure storage in EU regions. for Private you control region fully.
[06:20] Tom: Are there changes to backups? e.g., database snapshots — are they encrypted with the same DEK?
[06:25] Liam: yes snapshots are encrypted. backups follow the same envelope encryption flow; we maintain metadata about the wrapped DEK used for each snapshot.
[06:34] Priya: We require key rotation log entries for auditors. does the rewrap operation create an auditable event?
[06:39] Liam: yes, each rewrap is an auditable event with before/after key IDs, timestamp, actor, and operation ID.
[06:47] Tom: about HSM attestation — we need a chain of custody and attestation that keys never leave HSM. how do you handle that?
[06:54] Liam: for external HSMs, the HSM vendor provides attestation (e.g., hardware cert). Redwood can provide architecture diagrams and logs showing wrap/unwrap calls and attestations. if you want, we can set up a session with our HSM engineer to show the flow end-to-end.
[07:09] Samir: regarding encryption algorithms — AES-GCM? RSA? are there options for KMS to use AES-KW or RSA wrap?
[07:16] Liam: we support AES-GCM for data encryption and AES-KW / AES-KWP for key wrapping depending on the KMS. asymm wraps (RSA) are supported via the underlying KMS when available. we'll include a crypto spec in the docs.
[07:29] Priya: how long do logs persist and can we set retention to meet our policy?
[07:34] Maya: retention configurable in Private; for hosted we have tiers and can export logs to your storage to meet retention requirements.
[07:42] Tom: what about revocation? if a key is compromised, can you block access immediately and force rewrap?
[07:49] Liam: yes, you can revoke KEKs in your KMS which will block unwraps. we also support emergency rewrap and key rotation workflows to recover. revocation events also generate alerts/audit events.
[08:02] Priya: are there example threat models you can share that show risk surface for key compromise?
[08:07] Liam: yes we have threat models and runbooks for incident response — we'll share those.
[08:13] Samir: question on multi-tenant hosted deployments — if we use hosted but BYOK via cloud KMS, do we still have multi-tenant risk?
[08:21] Liam: BYOK reduces certain risks since KEKs stay in your KMS, but runtime resources are multi-tenant unless you go Dedicated or Private. for strict isolation Dedicated or Private is recommended.
[08:33] Tom: does Redwood support HSM pools shared across accounts or dedicated HSM per customer?
[08:38] Liam: we can do both in Private — you can provide a dedicated HSM cluster or use a shared vendor-managed pool with proper tenant isolation. for high-assurance customers we recommend dedicated HSM.
[08:51] Priya: curious about key escrow — do you ever escrow customer keys?
[08:56] Maya: we do not escrow keys for BYOK. if you want us to hold backup KEKs that's an explicit opt-in and comes with contractual controls. default is you hold the root.
[09:07] Tom: what about hardware-backed attestation for code running on nodes, e.g., remote attestation?
[09:12] Liam: for Private there's support for TPM-based attestation and we can discuss remote attestation options; for hosted it's tougher given shared infra but we can provide runtime provenance and image signing.
[09:24] Samir: anything else around compliance? backup location proof, third-party pen tests?
[09:30] Maya: we'll send SOC2 report, ISO27001 cert, and recent pen test summary. for deeper review we can arrange an NDA'd exchange of more artifacts.
[09:41] Priya: ok that's helpful. next, can we get an architecture doc that specifically shows BYOK flow with PKCS#11 for an on-prem HSM?
[09:48] Liam: yes, we'll include that. also we'll include a sample PKCS#11 config and how the Redwood runtime calls into the HSM for wrap/unwrap.
[09:58] Tom: one more on networking — for Private deployment, is egress IPSec or dedicated peering supported? we need to limit network paths that can reach the HSM.
[10:06] Liam: yes, Private supports VPC peering, private endpoints, and IPSec tunnels. you can restrict network paths and use security groups to limit access to HSM endpoints.
[10:18] Priya: any feature flags that are incompatible with BYOK? e.g., caching or smart routing?
[10:24] Liam: some caching features that rely on plaintext prefix operations may be limited if you keep all crypto client-side. smart routing still works; certain transparent cache optimizations require Redwood to have minimal plaintext access for prefixes. we can show feature-impact matrix.
[10:41] Samir: can you provide a sample SLA around key availability?
[10:45] Maya: for Dedicated/Private we can contract SLAs around key availability and define RTO/RPO for KMS endpoints. we'll draft language for the pilot contract.
[10:55] Tom: we're also evaluating HashiCorp Vault internally — curious how Redwood compares on BYOK story vs Vault.
[11:01] Liam: HashiCorp is a good internal KMS choice; Redwood focuses on integrating with customer KMS/HSM rather than replacing it. many customers use Vault for key lifecycle and plug it into Redwood.
[11:12] Priya: last question — are there any known past incidents related to key management we should be aware of?
[11:17] Maya: publicly none. we'll include a short incident summary and timeline for the last 18 months in the packet.
[11:24] (brief pause)
[11:30] Maya: ok to recap next steps — we'll send SOC2/ISO PDFs, the BYOK/HSM architecture doc, PKCS#11 samples, a short benchmark on unwrap latency, and schedule the HSM deep dive during week of April 27th.
[11:43] Tom: that works, please include the sample rewrap script and the audit log schema.
[11:49] Liam: will do.
[11:52] Priya: thanks, appreciate it.
[11:55] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up over email.

End of transcript.
